summary:
SPHEREx ATLAS – Discovering Motion Across the Infrared Sky

SPHEREx ATLAS is a public-facing astronomical exploration platform designed to help users investigate the changing infrared universe through NASA’s SPHEREx mission.

Users can search for astronomical targets, resolve their coordinates, and explore available SPHEREx archive observations through the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA). The platform presents observation metadata, including dates, wavelength coverage, and data availability.

Its interactive image-comparison workspace provides side-by-side, curtain, blend, and difference-map visualization modes, supported by quantitative measurements such as mean, RMS, peak difference, and changed-pixel metrics. These tools help users investigate potential variations between observations and identify patterns that may deserve further scientific study.

An integrated AI Research Assistant supports astronomical exploration by explaining scientific concepts and distinguishing direct observations, derived parameters, theoretical models, and unavailable information. English and Arabic interfaces make the platform accessible to a wider audience.

By combining astronomical target exploration, real archive discovery, interactive image analysis, and AI-assisted research, SPHEREx ATLAS aims to make infrared sky exploration more accessible and engaging for everyone.
RA/Dec search and chronological image playback reveal celestial motion over time.

SPHEREx ATLAS

Complete Project Architecture, Technologies & Implementation

1. Project Overview

SPHEREx ATLAS is a full-stack astronomical exploration and research platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It enables users to search astronomical targets, retrieve real SPHEREx observations, visualize FITS images, compare observations across different epochs, investigate infrared data, and interact with an AI-powered astronomy research assistant.

2. Technology Stack

Frontend

- React 19 – Component-based user interface.

- TypeScript – Type safety and maintainable application logic.

- Vite 8 – Development server and production build system.

- Tailwind CSS – Responsive styling and interface design.

- Lucide React – Interface icons.

- HTML5 Canvas – Scientific FITS image rendering and pixel visualization.

- Motion – Interface animations.

- Three.js – 3D visualization capabilities.

Backend

- Node.js – Server-side JavaScript runtime.

- Express.js – Backend routing and API middleware.

- Vite Middleware – Integrated development environment.

- TypeScript and TSX – Backend development and execution.

3. Astronomy Data Sources & APIs

The platform integrates with:

- NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA): Accesses SPHEREx observational data through the Table Access Protocol (TAP).

- ADQL: Executes spatial astronomical queries using Right Ascension and Declination coordinates.

- IVOA DataLink: Resolves links to downloadable astronomical data products.

- CDS Sesame / SIMBAD: Resolves astronomical target names into coordinates and catalog information.

- FITS: Retrieves and processes Flexible Image Transport System astronomical images.

- WCS: Supports World Coordinate System metadata for interpreting image coordinates.

4. Scientific Exploration Modules

Sky Explorer

- Searches astronomical targets and sky regions.

- Accepts astronomical coordinates and target names.

- Retrieves available archive observations.

- Displays observation metadata and data availability.

- Supports chronological observation exploration.

Target Resolution

- Resolves object names into astronomical coordinates.

- Provides catalog information and target identification.

Image Comparison

- Side-by-side comparison.

- Interactive curtain comparison.

- Image blending.

- Difference-map visualization.

- Mean, RMS, peak-difference, and changed-pixel measurements.

- Compatibility checks for image dimensions, WCS, filters, and units.

Spectral Studio

- Explores infrared spectral concepts and 102-band educational models.

- Supports data visualization and CSV/JSON exports.

Timeline Explorer

- Organizes available observations chronologically.

- Enables users to navigate observations across different epochs and investigate potential celestial motion or variation.

Saved Fields

- Provides access to saved astronomical search regions.

5. FITS Processing & Scientific Validation

The custom FITS engine, implemented in "src/services/fitsEngine.ts", supports astronomical image processing and Canvas-based rendering.

The backend validates FITS signatures and applies safeguards to archive downloads, including HTTPS host allowlisting, a 100 MB payload limit, and request-size and timeout controls.

Scientific provenance labels distinguish:

- REAL ARCHIVE DATA

- EXTERNAL CATALOG DATA

- SIMULATED DEMO DATA

- UNAVAILABLE DATA

This prevents simulated educational content from being confused with actual astronomical observations.

6. AI Research Assistant – Gemini API

The platform integrates the Google Gemini API through the official "@google/genai" JavaScript SDK.

Implementation details:

- Server-side API integration.

- Secure API key management through the "GEMINI_API_KEY" environment variable.

- Configurable model identification through "GEMINI_MODEL_ID".

- Dedicated research endpoint: "/api/gemini/research-assistant".

- Dedicated configuration endpoint: "/api/gemini/status".

- Structured scientific responses.

- Astronomy-focused system instructions.

- Error handling, timeout management, and retryability reporting.

- English and Arabic language support.

The assistant distinguishes:

- Direct Observations

- Derived Parameters

- Theoretical Models

- Missing / Unknown Information

The API key remains on the server and is never intended to be exposed in frontend code.

7. Application Architecture & Deployment

The application uses a React frontend connected to backend API services.

Local development uses Express and Vite middleware through "server.ts". Production API endpoints are deployed through Vercel, with environment variables configured in the deployment settings.

The source code is maintained on GitHub and deployed to Vercel.

Production domain: "https://www.spherexatlas.earth"

8. Development, Testing & Build Tools

- npm – Dependency and package management.

- TypeScript Compiler – Static type checking.

- "npm run lint" – Type checking.

- "npm run build" – Production build.

- "npm test" – Automated FITS engine, scientific comparison, offline integration, and security tests.

- Git and GitHub – Version control and source management.

- Vercel – Production hosting and serverless API deployment.

9. Scientific Integrity

SPHEREx ATLAS separates real archive observations from simulated demonstration data. Its architecture is designed to make astronomical data exploration accessible while preserving data provenance, validation, and transparency about scientific limitations.

Project Goal: Bridge the gap between complex infrared astronomical datasets and public scientific discovery through interactive visualization, accessible research tools, and AI-assisted exploration.
